note: Study-supplement source on the wording axis, .sav column names on the code axis, reconciled against the data and against the instrument's own published scoring key. The IRW item codes ARE the S2 File .sav column names (data/ozkurt_2026_wrestlers.py melts columns matching r'EGOQ\d+$' with var_name='item' and renames nothing), but the .sav's variable labels carry only subdimension+ordinal ('Task orientation G1'..'Ego orientation E5'), not wording -- so the words come from S6 File Table 2, which lists all 10 items against an 'Original item no.' column, 1..10. mapping_basis=paper_explicit for that reason. VERIFICATION (see verify_ozkurt_2026_ego_orientation.R, VERDICT: PASS): (a) live IRW per-item 1-5 response counts equal the .sav's cell for cell, 10/10; (b) S1 File .xlsx holds the same 374 respondents under headers that NUMBER the columns '2.Ego Orientation'..'10.Ego Orientation'; rows are permuted between the deposits, so the columns were tied by their 5-level count vectors, which give a unique bijection -- each numbered header matches exactly one of EGOQ2..EGOQ10 and no other (9/9; EGOQ1 has no S1 column because that deposit omits item 1, and falls out by elimination); (c) the .sav variable label, S6's Subdimension column and the GOEM's own published scoring key (Task = items 1,3,4,6,9; Ego = items 2,5,7,8,10, from exercise-motivation.bangor.ac.uk/goem/goemmain.php) agree for all 10 -- the third of these was not written by the study's authors, so the numbering is not resting on their own files alone; (d) S6's 10 items pair one-for-one AND IN ORDER with the 10 items of the canonical GOEM questionnaire PDF, matching verb and target item by item (1 'do my best during exercise' / 'I exercise to the best of my ability'; 2 'others cannot exercise as well as I can' / 'Other exercisers don't do as well as me'; 3 'make progress'; 4 'achieve the exercise goals I have set for myself'; 5 'show other exercisers that I am the best' / 'I can show other exercisers that I'm better than everyone else'; 6 'make improvements' / 'I feel like I've improved'; 7 'prove to myself that I am the only one who can perform a particular exercise'; 8 'more ability than other exercisers' / 'more capable than other exercisers'; 9 'a level that reflects my personal improvement'; 10 'prove to others that I am the best'). WORDING: S6's English is the authors' own rendering of their Turkish administration and diverges from the canonical GOEM in a consistent way -- every item is recast as a self-contained 'I feel good when...' sentence, whereas the GOEM form puts a shared stem ('In my physical activity, I would feel / do feel that things go well when...') in front of bare clauses. The S6 wording is shipped verbatim, so no separate stem is recorded in instructions. ANCHORS: S6 states '10 items rated on a 5-point Likert scale ranging from 1 = Strongly Disagree to 5 = Strongly Agree', which is also the canonical GOEM anchoring; direction corroborated by the data (task-block items 1,3,4,6,9 mean 4.46-4.70 while ego-block items 2,5,7,8,10 mean 3.26-4.22 -- the reversed reading would have national-team wrestlers disagreeing that they feel good when they do their best or improve, and would invert the task/ego gap). Points 2, 3 and 4 are unlabelled in every source, so their option_text is deliberately blank rather than padded with their own numbers. instructions and section_prompt are blank deliberately: neither the article nor any of the seven supplementary files publishes an administered instruction stem. LANGUAGE: administered in Turkish (374 wrestlers under the Turkish Wrestling Federation; Turkish adaptation by Ersoz et al., 2017). The Turkish wording appears in NONE of the deposit files -- S1 .xlsx headers are English subscale labels, S2 .sav's 71 variable labels are all English, S6 prints only English items, S7 is a demographic codebook -- so the Step-4 English fallback applies: English in the base fields, language=Turkish, _translated columns omitted rather than emitted empty, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied. The Ersoz et al. (2017) Turkish validation paper is CC BY 4.0 but is off-source and was bot-walled at tandfonline/cogentoa (403 on both the VOR PDF links Crossref advertises), and per Step 4 recoverability is scoped to the deposit and the paper's own supplements, so the fallback was taken rather than hunting further. STEP 3b -- NAME MISMATCH: the table is named 'ego_orientation' and the dictionary Description calls it the 'Ego Orientation Questionnaire (10 items)', but the live data are the WHOLE 10-item EGOQ, five task-orientation items (EGOQ1,3,4,6,9) and five ego-orientation items (EGOQ2,5,7,8,10). The instrument field names the full questionnaire accordingly; see notes for the Description fix. RIGHTS: ships. The GOEM is not in instrument_rights_register.csv and no restriction is quotable from its rights holder: the instrument's own site (School of Sport, Health & Exercise Sciences, Bangor University; D. Markland) publishes the full questionnaire for free download in PDF and Word from a downloads page that states no fee, no permission requirement, no non-commercial and no no-derivatives or no-redistribution term -- the page's only rights text is the site-wide 'Copyright (c) Bangor University' footer, which is a notice and not a condition (the PANAS case). Silence is permission, so it ships. In any case the wording IRW copied is the CC BY 4.0 PLOS supplement's, and a register row for the GOEM was not written because the register is a shared file and parallel agents are active this round.
public_note: Despite the table name, this is the complete 10-item Exercise Goal Orientation Questionnaire: five of the items (EGOQ1, EGOQ3, EGOQ4, EGOQ6, EGOQ9) measure task orientation rather than ego orientation, following the instrument's own published scoring key. The item text shipped here is English, but the study administered a Turkish adaptation (Ersoz et al., 2017) and published no Turkish wording in any of its seven supplementary files; the English is the authors' own rendering from their S6 File, which pairs one-for-one and in order with the 10 items of the original GOEM (Petherick & Markland, 2008). Only the two endpoints of the 1-5 response scale are labelled (1 = Strongly Disagree, 5 = Strongly Agree); points 2, 3 and 4 are blank because no source labels them, and no instructions are given because none were published

INSTRUMENT identified with certainty, not by name match: the paper's Measures section states 'Sport Motivation Scale-II (SMS-II), developed by Pelletier and colleagues and adapted into Turkish by Yildiz and colleagues ... consists of 16 items rated on a 7-point Likert scale and includes six subdimensions: intrinsic regulation, integrated regulation, identified regulation, introjected regulation, external regulation, and amotivation', and the S2 File .sav's own variable labels for SMS1..SMS16 are exactly those six subscale names with the item number appended ('Introjected regulation1', 'Amotivation2', 'Integrated regulation3', ...), 16/16. STEP 3b CLEAN: 16 live items SMS1..SMS16, resp {1..7}, n=374 each, matching the paper's stated 16 items / 7-point scale / N=374 exactly, so the table is the SMS-II and not a sibling scale from the same battery. RIGHTS TEST (SKILL 'Rights on the wording', as restated 2026-09-08 after irw#1945): the SMS-II is part of the Center for Self-Determination Theory questionnaire library, and its originators include Deci and Ryan. The CSDT Limited Use License RESERVES RIGHTS rather than disclaiming fitness -- quoted: 'the Organization hereby grants to User, a non-exclusive, non-transferable, limited use license to use the Materials solely for non-for-profit research purposes. User covenants and agrees that User shall not: (i) use the Materials ... for any commercial or for-profit purposes ...; (ii) make available or distribute all or any portion of the Materials to any third party; ... (v) publish the Materials online in any form, without the prior written consent of the Organization.' (https://selfdeterminationtheory.org/terms-and-conditions/, sha256 fe92eda1...5ab10d, fetched 2026-09-08 by the register). Non-commercial + no-redistribution + no-online-publication are three reserved rights, any one of which blocks; IRW redistributes, so 'our own use is non-profit academic research' is not a defence. Ben's 2026-09-09 FULL SCOPE ruling on that register row is directly on point: the licence reaches every instrument in the CSDT library, NOT only wording downloaded from selfdeterminationtheory.org, and reaches translations and adaptations, so the Turkish Yildiz et al. adaptation administered here is a derivative and is covered. The PLOS article's CC BY 4.0 licence governs the response data, not the item wording -- a CC BY deposit does not launder a restricted instrument. Register row applied, not re-derived; no new escalation and no contact with the rights holder (Shipley rule). BLOCK IS EFFECTIVE, not cosmetic: the IRW item codes are SMS1..SMS16 and the .sav variable labels carry only subscale names, so no SMS-II wording is already exposed through the response table. The extraction was otherwise fully solvable -- the code derivation is 'item IS the source column name' (data/ozkurt_2026_wrestlers.py melts columns matching ^SMS\d+$ with no rename), so the mapping would have been authoritative at the source; only rights stop it. RETRY TEST: NO -- a determinate verdict, not an access failure. Every source needed was reached (paper, S2 File .sav, processing script, rights register). An unchanged retry now would reach the same block.
